items.title: Mississauga: Parrish and Crombie Tied; City Mood Turns Negative
items.summary: Carolyn Parrish and Bonnie Crombie are tied at 35% among decided and leaning voters, while more Mississauga residents say the city is moving in the wrong direction than the right direction. August 14, 2026 (Mississauga, ON) - A new Liaison Strategies Mississauga survey shows Mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie tied among decided and leaning voters, while the city's overall mood has turned negative. If a mayoral election were held today, Parrish and Crombie would each receive 35% among decided and leaning voters, followed by Dipika Damerla at 18% and Alvin Tedjo at 12%. Among all voters, Parrish and Crombie are tied at 26% each, followed by Damerla at 13% and Tedjo at 9%. Twenty-six per cent are undecided. The survey also finds that 46% of Mississauga residents say the city is moving in the wrong direction, compared to 32% who say it is moving in the right direction and 22% who are not sure. Parrish's job approval is slightly underwater: 38% approve of the job she is doing as mayor, 42% disapprove, and 20% are not sure. Liaison surveyed a random sample of 1,000 Mississauga residents from August 11 to August 12, 2026, using Interactive Voice Recording (IVR) technology. Participants were reached through random digit dialling (RDD) across both landline and cellular phone networks. The resulting data was weighted to match targets based on the 2021 Census. 1 percentage points, 19 times out of 20. The margin is higher for sub-samples. Totals may not add up to 100% due to rounding. Liaison Strategies is one of the most accurate polling firms in Canada.

items.title: Doug Ford backed Carolyn Parrish for Mississauga mayor. A new poll suggests it’s backfiring
items.summary: A new poll shows Carolyn Parrish and Bonnie Crombie tied in Mississauga, with voters split on police spending A new poll suggests Bonnie Crombie and Carolyn Parrish are tied in the race to become Mississauga’s next mayor. The current and former mayors of Mississauga appear to be neck and neck in the race for the city’s top job, with a new poll also suggesting an equal number of voters are unsure of who to choose. The poll from Liaison Strategies released Friday suggests that if the Oct. 26 mayoral election were held today, Carolyn Parrish and Bonnie Crombie would each earn 26 per cent of decided voters — with another 26 per cent undecided. The two other leading candidates, current councillors Dipika Damerla and Alvin Tedjo, would get 13 per cent and nine per cent of decided voters, respectively. “None of them have made a clear-cut argument for why it should be them compared to the others,” said Liaison principal David Valentin, noting there are a lot of voters available to win over and a feeling the city is heading in the wrong direction. ” Registration opens Friday for candidates in this fall's municipal elections, and two contenders in Mississauga already have a clear idea what some Registration opens Friday for candidates in this fall's municipal elections, and two contenders in Mississauga already have a clear idea what some An October 2025 poll from Liaison also found a tie in the then-hypothetical battle between Crombie — who left her job as mayor to become Ontario Liberal Leader, only to resign after the latest provincial election — and Parrish, who replaced Crombie in a 2024 byelection.

items.title: City Warns E-Scooter Injuries Among Mississauga Kids Have Doubled in a Year
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, officials are reminding parents to keep children off e-scooters and e-bikes after a national report found 10 kids died from related injuries across Canada last year, six of them in Ontario. The city cites Canadian Paediatric Surveillance Program data showing 57 severe paediatric cases nationwide in 2025 involving death, an ICU admission or a hospital stay longer than two days, including 12 ICU admissions and 26 hospital stays beyond two days. The City of Mississauga notes e-scooters can be a convenient way for residents and visitors aged 16 and older to get around without a car, helping people connect to transit, school or work. But the city says local emergency department visits involving children aged 15 and under on e-scooters more than doubled between 2023 and 2024, rising from 34 visits to 72. Mississauga officials are using those numbers to urge parents to keep young children off the devices even as their popularity grows.

items.title: Behind the Angled Facade on Mississauga Road: The Leslie Log House Marks 200 Years
items.summary: According to Modern Mississauga Media, the Leslie Log House on Mississauga Road is celebrating its 200th anniversary this year, having been built in 1826 by John Leslie Sr. and his wife, Esther Leslie. The outlet reports the house sits at a slight angle to the road, with its front door facing away from traffic, and is surrounded by a remnant orchard left over from the former Riviere Fruit Farm. Modern Mississauga Media notes the building was relocated to its current site in 1994 and is now owned by the City of Mississauga, serving as home to the Streetsville Historical Society and Archives. The outlet's history of the house traces Esther Leslie's own story, noting she was born in 1782 in County Tyrone, Ireland, and first married a man named William Leslie while he was stationed there. Mississauga marked the log house's bicentennial with a public event on Saturday, Aug. 8.

items.title: DavidsTea returns to Square One after closing 6 years ago in Mississauga
items.summary: Tea lovers rejoice — DavidsTea is back in Square One Shopping Centre in Mississauga. The tea merchant officially announced the reopening in a press release today. “We are delighted to bring the full DavidsTea experience to consumers at Square One with our premium tea collections, wide assortment of accessories and expert recommendations from our Tea Guides,” said Sarah Segal, the company’s chief executive officer and chief brand officer. The shop, located on level two by entrance eight in Square One, celebrated their grand opening on Aug. 2. “A huge thank you to everyone who came by our opening event at Square One,” DavidsTea said on Instagram. ” Customers seemed thrilled with the shop’s return. “So happy to have you back close to home,” one person wrote on Instagram. “The store is beautiful and the staff is amazing! ” DavidsTea shut down 82 locations across Canada amid financial struggles in 2020, but last year the company announced a comeback. Stores were planned for Quebec City, Montreal and a location opened at the Oshawa Centre in June.

items.title: Mississauga Shelter Staff Say the $25 Adoption Push Isn't Skipping Any Steps
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, staff at Mississauga Animal Services say the screening process for adopting a pet hasn't changed during the shelter's ongoing $25 adoption event, even as the reduced fee draws more interest. The discount, running until Aug. 22 at the shelter's Central Parkway West location, cuts the standard adoption cost from roughly $280 plus tax for dogs and puppies and up to $190 plus tax for cats and kittens down to a flat $25. Greg Madeley, the shelter's manager of animal care and wellbeing, told Mississauga.com the lower price is meant to free up kennel space, not shortcut the process of matching an animal with the right home. Mississauga.com reports staff still take steps before an animal leaves the shelter to make sure the pet and the prospective owner are a good fit. Among the animals up for adoption is Kaito, a senior dog who has been at the shelter since July 2023. Mississauga.com notes the shelter has taken in 18,986 animals since 2021.

items.title: Halton Police Say a Mississauga Man Filmed a Woman in an Oakville Fitting Room
items.summary: According to INsauga, Halton Regional Police have charged a Mississauga man after a woman reported being filmed inside a change room at the Winners store on Winston Churchill Boulevard in Oakville on July 22. Police say the woman confronted the man after noticing him, but he fled the store before officers arrived. INsauga reports investigators later identified and arrested the suspect, 34-year-old Jeffrey Abou-Mechrek of Mississauga, charging him with one count of voyeurism. He was released with a future court date in Milton. Police released a photo of Abou-Mechrek because investigators are concerned there may be additional victims they haven't yet identified. Anyone who believes they may have been victimized, or who has information about the case, is asked to contact Halton's 2 District Criminal Investigations Bureau.

items.title: Brampton landlord to face jail time after fire that killed pregnant woman, child in 2023
items.summary: An Ontario landlord has been sentenced to jail time after being convicted of seven charges following a Brampton fire that left a pregnant woman and her daughter dead more than three years ago.

items.title: Construction on Hazel McCallion LRT to continue into 2027 in Mississauga
items.summary: Construction on the Hazel McCallion LRT in Mississauga is expected to continue for at least one more year. The 18-kilometre light-rail line will feature 19 stops along Hurontario Street from Port Credit GO in Mississauga to the Brampton Gateway Terminal at Steeles Avenue. During a Tuesday announcement marking completion of tunnelling on the Eglinton Crosstown West extension, Michael Lindsay, Metrolinx’s president and CEO, provided updates on the Hazel McCallion LRT. Lindsay said 75 per cent of the track work is done, eight out of 14 traction power substations are energized and the maintenance and storage facility is energized. “We hope to have all civil infrastructure on this project complete by roughly this time next year,” Lindsay said. Once that construction is complete, the project will enter the testing phase, he added. Mississauga officials, who’ve long expressed frustration at project delays, have said the project is hurting businesses and testing drivers’ patience daily. com it wouldn’t surprise her if the new LRT route didn’t take its first passengers until 2029.
